descripcion: At B1 you use a/an, the and no article correctly, plus common quantifiers like some, any, much and many. These small words are used constantly and often skipped by Spanish speakers, whose language uses articles differently.

filas: The dog next door barks a lot.
I have some time. Do you have any questions?

ejemplos.texto: I saw a dog in the park this morning.
The dog next door barks a lot at night.
Do you have any questions about this?

notas: The is used when both speaker and listener know which thing is meant.
Some is used in positive sentences, any in questions and negatives.
Much goes with uncountable nouns, many with countable plural nouns.

contraste.es: El español usa artículos de forma más generalizada, incluso con sustantivos abstractos o plurales generales (me gusta la música). El inglés omite el artículo en esos casos (I like music), lo cual es una fuente constante de error para hispanohablantes.

errores: Adding the before a general or abstract noun where English uses no article.
Using any in a positive statement instead of some.

traducciones.fr: Il n’y a pas beaucoup de…
Il n’y a pas beaucoup de…

autochequeo: Have I avoided the before general or abstract nouns?
Is some used in positive sentences and any in questions/negatives?
Are much and many used with the right kind of noun?
Does the sentence sound natural, not translated word for word?
